{/*cf-review:field-05ed470265b94e8696d5dba25a546905*/"If your small team repeatedly answers the same questions and has current, approved answers, try drafting routine replies for a person to check. AI can also sort enquiries or find information for staff. You do not need to buy a public-facing chatbot to try it. Choose a narrow task and name its reviewer."}

{/*cf-review:field-eeaa3ece5e4e49cc96f1e5b32032b7da*/"Generative AI produces content from instructions and supplied information. Fluent wording does not establish that an answer is correct. The Australian Government\u2019s business.gov.au guidance recommends identifying a business problem before choosing a tool."}

{CF_REVIEW_b316b0dd159e4a34bef9da0edc72b60d}

{/*cf-review:field-71b7f9a3e43d4230ba0975f14c6aae80*/"Choose a task that repeats often enough to investigate, with answers your team can verify. Use your enquiry history and documents to compare workflow fit. The worksheet makes no product recommendations or savings promises."}

{/*cf-review:field-451ed7df8fda4dc5aff9463bf62a2e99*/"Copy the comparison and pilot record into your working notes."}

{/*cf-review:field-72de0e972011470f9d1dd7de02d4525e*/"Compare the options"}

{/*cf-review:field-270a5daa88024e9cb2d21133b38c5bc4*/"Reply drafting from frequently asked questions (FAQs) suits repeated routine enquiries with current, approved answers. Limit inputs to non-identifying question text and public facts. Manual draft-only testing avoids inbox integration. Without review, misstated instructions or policy could reach a customer."}

{/*cf-review:field-4756b11d2c1848f78217bd7bd84661f3*/"Enquiry triage means sorting enquiries for the right person. Consider it when sorting a queue consumes staff time and you have clear categories and routing rules. Incoming messages may contain personal or sensitive information. Staff-checked labels avoid automatic routing, but a wrong label could delay an urgent or sensitive enquiry."}

{/*cf-review:field-1eb59582348443ddb31a95e647acf7de*/"Internal knowledge lookup suits repeated staff searches through maintained, authoritative documents. Confidential material may need restricted access. Preparing a small permitted document set differs from integrating a whole knowledge system. An incorrect answer could lead staff to follow the wrong procedure."}

{/*cf-review:field-95314867e7a34b55800a267f769be1e9*/"Record your pilot"}

{/*cf-review:field-0d704cdcae8044a999a15a1c7bf132b1*/"Defer if volume is low, sources conflict, review capacity is absent or data handling cannot be approved. Improving FAQs or using saved replies may be enough."}

  • {/*cf-review:field-09a96384f8d643c4b04b3374591d4386*/"Record the chosen task or deferral, rationale, scope and exclusions."}
  • {/*cf-review:field-8728da32f8ec4d84a27a3856141f2bfd*/"Name the accountable owner and reviewer, and list outstanding approvals."}
  • {/*cf-review:field-cf8a935f92e94fd4a4b7c87809145ccc*/"Identify the approved tool and settings, source versions, permitted data and approval status."}
  • {/*cf-review:field-929ac57a838c4ece8b453f80be124926*/"Record manual handling measures and a comparable sample for the baseline."}
  • {/*cf-review:field-a85d3e659efc4513aa0159d170eaf421*/"Set dates, a case cap, a staff-hour cap and an A$ spending cap."}
  • {/*cf-review:field-135b20fc33a042e79085849dcfd5be9d*/"Specify approval before sending, escalation reasons and the human decision-maker."}
  • {/*cf-review:field-6020740f91154421984b1153fdb321a2*/"Set numerical success thresholds using the measures below."}
  • {/*cf-review:field-3c88dc5878fe4cea8618ba01577391cf*/"Define stop triggers, a rollback owner and the return-to-manual process."}

{CF_REVIEW_80c56934f3854ad3895703addc529dd7}

{/*cf-review:field-19cd17cd35cb4cf7a4419f48b3dfe643*/"Name someone responsible for the source material and collect a small, dated set of approved facts. Resolve conflicting FAQ pages before including those questions in the pilot; the model must not decide which policy is correct."}

{/*cf-review:field-d25252f36dc44290a5b0cb778400a073*/"Before approving a tool, check how the vendor handles inputs and outputs: whether they can be used for model training, where they are stored, who can access them, and how retention and deletion work. A paid subscription alone does not establish suitability."}

{/*cf-review:field-7f639b33077e43a2af049063dedfea4d*/"Consult the Office of the Australian Information Commissioner\u2019s guidance on commercially available AI products and seek appropriate professional guidance about Australian privacy obligations that apply to your business."}

{/*cf-review:field-be6ffe484c4946a0a9ed6fba0c51729f*/"Before testing, name the reviewer and the person who handles exceptions. Require the reviewer to check every reply against approved sources and correct it before sending, consistent with business.gov.au\u2019s advice to verify AI-generated information against trustworthy sources. Refunds, complaints, sensitive enquiries and answers the sources cannot support must go to the named human decision-maker. Keep sending under human control: the AI must not independently promise a refund, approve an exception or make another commitment to a customer."}

{/*cf-review:field-a3b36cc76ac64c60b4f6980d466b910e*/"If an enquiry cannot be prepared within the agreed data boundaries, keep it in the existing manual workflow until the accountable owner resolves the approval."}
{"Do not enter confidential or personal customer information into unapproved tools. Until the tool and intended data use are approved, prepare with fictional enquiries and approved public facts."}

{CF_REVIEW_a07c49effab340b7b0c7c2115e2cacdd}

{/*cf-review:field-0812e66c7b83497389c7769d55a59b87*/"Chatbase\u2019s customer-service guide recommends tracking response time, escalation and quality. Use the proposed measures below for your draft-only pilot, without treating vendor claims as benchmarks."}

{/*cf-review:field-c013bc682cc5447e8f4c5d1fa00e65a3*/"Compare the whole task"}

{/*cf-review:field-6c5bd2527bd14f32b81d56640e26ac87*/"Your baseline is the current manual process measured before introducing AI. Compare similar routine enquiries using identical start and finish points. Assisted handling time includes preparation, prompting, waiting that occupies staff, review, correction, handover and sending. Track setup and training separately, but include them in total pilot effort. Generation speed alone is not a fair comparison."}

{/*cf-review:field-b00a5c81f18d4b1e8d55bf378f1823c1*/"Calculate draft accuracy as drafts whose factual claims and necessary instructions match approved sources without factual correction, divided by all drafts reviewed. Record serious errors separately."}

{/*cf-review:field-1444b9c0b7364337b2cbe17b89300c96*/"Calculate escalation frequency as cases requiring an additional human decision or handoff, divided by all cases entering the pilot workflow. Routine draft review is not escalation. Record reasons and missed required escalations: a lower rate can conceal failures to seek help."}

{/*cf-review:field-455c662ee3324f6193c6bdf103ee4d6f*/"Total pilot cost is incremental tool and usage charges plus staff time at a declared hourly cost. Include all pilot effort, including escalations, without counting staff minutes twice. Show cash spending and labour cost separately."}

{/*cf-review:field-41b1c8771edf464da98f7e37d0212ad9*/"Decide what would justify continuing"}

{/*cf-review:field-6d67ef7ac70c449db3e43ff0d7401510*/"Set numerical thresholds for handling time, draft accuracy, escalation performance and cost before testing. Specify critical safety failures and approval breaches that require an immediate stop, alongside case, time and spending limits. If a stop condition occurs, return to the manual process and investigate before proposing another trial."}

{/*cf-review:field-72e05e1f475145d9918607deddff69d9*/"Continue only when the agreed quality, safety, time and cost conditions are met. If too few eligible enquiries arrive before the deadline, record an inconclusive result. Extending the trial requires a new decision. A small sample can inform your next local decision; it cannot establish a general productivity claim."}

{CF_REVIEW_acb063f7986f41b68f47e6a58a5d9c21}

{/*cf-review:field-ca61e50da2ed4e66b1786a9674cf0f6c*/"Suppose a small software startup chooses reply drafting for recurring questions about exporting reports. These illustrative limits and thresholds are not industry standards, tested results or MLAI customer evidence. Drafting suits this workload better than enquiry sorting or internal lookup because questions repeat and maintained public instructions provide a narrow source set."}

{/*cf-review:field-a7629ba907f94d17a383c59b40ae18ac*/"The founder owns the pilot, excluding account-specific troubleshooting and all mandatory-escalation cases described above. Before assisted testing, the team measures comparable manual handling times, leaving the baseline result blank until measured."}

{/*cf-review:field-fd75b63ddb774cd48d6d483c03709164*/"The proposed limits are two weeks, 20 eligible draft cases, four hours of total staff time and A$50 in incremental tool charges. At an assumed labour cost of A$50 per hour, the combined budget ceiling is A$250. These budget choices do not represent vendor prices or predicted expenditure."}

{/*cf-review:field-3d92db99f86f4eea8bff38da4f941d03*/"The team prepares fictional questions and a dated, approved public help-page extract. After recording tool and data approvals, it enters only approved, non-identifying task text from eligible live enquiries into the approved tool. The founder checks every draft against the extract, corrects it and manually sends the final reply. The AI receives no inbox send permission. Anything outside scope goes to the named human decision-maker."}

{/*cf-review:field-21869505ba814570b6f4519d745c313a*/"The record uses the handling-time, accuracy, escalation and cost measures above. Setup and training count towards the staff-time limit."}

{/*cf-review:field-08fae076743748b4955913c8359a71d1*/"Before starting, the founder records the continue conditions: at least a 20% reduction in median total handling time against the measured baseline, at least 19 of 20 drafts factually correct without correction, no missed mandatory escalations and costs within the agreed limits. An unplanned handoff rate above 20% prompts a scope review, never pressure to avoid necessary escalation."}

{/*cf-review:field-18e7429e145a4c46b02bca55771527d3*/"The founder handles rollback and investigation if a stop condition occurs. Time or spending limits also end testing. The output is a proposed pilot record ready for approval, with results unfilled. Meeting the conditions would justify considering another bounded test, not automatically launching a public chatbot."}

{CF_REVIEW_1a3ebf2c00ca44a999900aa01745ac38}

{/*cf-review:field-fe5bb56519b64f368dfb68261e6dec92*/"Keep your pilot plan in draft until the named owner resolves outstanding approvals. You can discuss the chosen use case or documented decision to defer before committing money or connecting customer systems."}

{/*cf-review:field-6c2bc98c97f14cee94dac7e8056dd4a9*/"Ask peers about their own trials: which corrections consumed the most time, which vendor data controls did they verify, and what made them stop or narrow the trial? Use their answers to question your assumptions. Another business\u2019s experience is not proof that your plan will work."}

{/*cf-review:field-a0b5d7df11ee4755bc782469b4285221*/"Explore MLAI events for optional peer learning. Availability, format and cost depend on the organiser\u2019s event page. Attendance does not guarantee one-to-one implementation advice or replace running a pilot."}

editorial_brief.reader_task: Choose one low-risk customer-service AI use case for an Australian startup and draft a small, measurable pilot plan with human review before buying tools or services.
editorial_brief.distinct_contribution: Provide a beginner-friendly decision worksheet that compares FAQ reply drafting, enquiry triage and internal knowledge lookup, then walks through a hypothetical pilot for drafting replies to routine enquiries. Help readers define approved source material, data boundaries, human approval, baseline measures and stop-or-continue rules rather than defaulting to a public-facing chatbot.
acceptance_criteria: Address Australian startup owners with small teams, limited budgets and no dedicated AI function; explain technical terms in plain language.

Compare the three use cases by enquiry volume, availability of reliable source material, data sensitivity, implementation effort and consequences of an incorrect answer; include a valid decision to defer AI.
Include a reusable pilot-plan worksheet covering scope, accountable owner, approved tools and data, baseline, time and spending limits, review process, success thresholds and rollback.
Use a clearly labelled hypothetical reply-drafting example, with every reply reviewed by a person before sending; do not imply that tests, research or customer results have already been obtained.
Explain how to measure handling time including review and correction, answer accuracy against approved sources, escalation frequency and total pilot cost; have readers set thresholds before starting.

Specify that confidential or personal customer data must not be entered into unapproved tools. Cover checking vendor data handling, access controls and retention, and seeking appropriate guidance on applicable Australian privacy obligations without giving personalised legal advice.
Keep refunds, complaints, sensitive enquiries and unsupported answers subject to explicit human escalation; do not recommend autonomous commitments to customers.

End the practical workflow with a shortlisted use case, a draft pilot plan and questions for peers. Only then offer 'Explore MLAI events' at '/events' as an optional business next action, separate from the reader's task.
State that event availability, format and cost depend on the organiser's event page, and that attendance does not guarantee one-to-one implementation advice or replace running a pilot.

# How Australian Startups Can Test AI for Customer Service Choose a customer-service AI use case and draft a small pilot with data limits, human review, clear measures and a stop rule before buying tools. ![Two people look at an open laptop, one gesturing with a hand and the other wearing glasses. A leafy plant is behind them.](https://firebasestorage.googleapis.com/v0/b/mlai-main-website.firebasestorage.app/o/content-factory%2FU05QPB483K9%2FMLAI-AUS-Inc%2Fmlai-au%2Fimages%2Fhero-558630ed-22eb-4360-88be-6f4da76ee87e.jpg?alt=media&token=cbaf1473-25d5-4ad9-958e-7a5b160f1be1) *Choose a customer-service AI use case and draft a small pilot with data limits, human review, clear measures and a stop rule before buying tools.* ## Quick answers ### Can I use AI for customer service? AI can draft routine replies, sort enquiries or find information for staff. Reply drafting is a candidate when questions repeat, approved answers are current and a person checks every response before sending. ### When should a startup defer customer-service AI? Defer AI when enquiry volume is low, source documents conflict, no reviewer is available or data handling cannot be approved. Improving FAQs or using saved replies remains a valid alternative. ### What should a customer-service AI pilot measure? Measure complete handling time, draft accuracy against approved sources, escalation frequency and total cost, including staff effort. Set success thresholds and stop rules before testing, with review and correction included in the workload.

In this article

  1. Start with routine reply drafts
  2. Choose a use case and draft its pilot record
  3. Approve the information and the human handover
  4. Set the measures before you start
  5. A hypothetical pilot for routine reply drafts
  6. Take a draft plan to your next conversation

package.article_html:
How Australian Startups Can Test AI for Customer Service

Choose a customer-service AI use case and draft a small pilot with data limits, human review, clear measures and a stop rule before buying tools.

Quick answers

Can I use AI for customer service?

AI can draft routine replies, sort enquiries or find information for staff. Reply drafting is a candidate when questions repeat, approved answers are current and a person checks every response before sending.

When should a startup defer customer-service AI?

Defer AI when enquiry volume is low, source documents conflict, no reviewer is available or data handling cannot be approved. Improving FAQs or using saved replies remains a valid alternative.

What should a customer-service AI pilot measure?

Measure complete handling time, draft accuracy against approved sources, escalation frequency and total cost, including staff effort. Set success thresholds and stop rules before testing, with review and correction included in the workload.

In this article

  1. Start with routine reply drafts
  2. Choose a use case and draft its pilot record
  3. Approve the information and the human handover
  4. Set the measures before you start
  5. A hypothetical pilot for routine reply drafts
  6. Take a draft plan to your next conversation

Start with routine reply drafts

If your small team repeatedly answers the same questions and has current, approved answers, try drafting routine replies for a person to check. AI can also sort enquiries or find information for staff. You do not need to buy a public-facing chatbot to try it. Choose a narrow task and name its reviewer.

Generative AI produces content from instructions and supplied information. Fluent wording does not establish that an answer is correct. The Australian Government’s business.gov.au guidance recommends identifying a business problem before choosing a tool.

Choose a use case and draft its pilot record

Choose a task that repeats often enough to investigate, with answers your team can verify. Use your enquiry history and documents to compare workflow fit. The worksheet makes no product recommendations or savings promises.

Copy the comparison and pilot record into your working notes.

Compare the options

Reply drafting from frequently asked questions (FAQs) suits repeated routine enquiries with current, approved answers. Limit inputs to non-identifying question text and public facts. Manual draft-only testing avoids inbox integration. Without review, misstated instructions or policy could reach a customer.

Enquiry triage means sorting enquiries for the right person. Consider it when sorting a queue consumes staff time and you have clear categories and routing rules. Incoming messages may contain personal or sensitive information. Staff-checked labels avoid automatic routing, but a wrong label could delay an urgent or sensitive enquiry.

Internal knowledge lookup suits repeated staff searches through maintained, authoritative documents. Confidential material may need restricted access. Preparing a small permitted document set differs from integrating a whole knowledge system. An incorrect answer could lead staff to follow the wrong procedure.

Record your pilot

Defer if volume is low, sources conflict, review capacity is absent or data handling cannot be approved. Improving FAQs or using saved replies may be enough.

  • Record the chosen task or deferral, rationale, scope and exclusions.
  • Name the accountable owner and reviewer, and list outstanding approvals.
  • Identify the approved tool and settings, source versions, permitted data and approval status.
  • Record manual handling measures and a comparable sample for the baseline.
  • Set dates, a case cap, a staff-hour cap and an A$ spending cap.
  • Specify approval before sending, escalation reasons and the human decision-maker.
  • Set numerical success thresholds using the measures below.
  • Define stop triggers, a rollback owner and the return-to-manual process.

Approve the information and the human handover

Name someone responsible for the source material and collect a small, dated set of approved facts. Resolve conflicting FAQ pages before including those questions in the pilot; the model must not decide which policy is correct.

Before approving a tool, check how the vendor handles inputs and outputs: whether they can be used for model training, where they are stored, who can access them, and how retention and deletion work. A paid subscription alone does not establish suitability.

Consult the Office of the Australian Information Commissioner’s guidance on commercially available AI products and seek appropriate professional guidance about Australian privacy obligations that apply to your business.

Before testing, name the reviewer and the person who handles exceptions. Require the reviewer to check every reply against approved sources and correct it before sending, consistent with business.gov.au’s advice to verify AI-generated information against trustworthy sources. Refunds, complaints, sensitive enquiries and answers the sources cannot support must go to the named human decision-maker. Keep sending under human control: the AI must not independently promise a refund, approve an exception or make another commitment to a customer.

When an enquiry falls outside the data boundary

If an enquiry cannot be prepared within the agreed data boundaries, keep it in the existing manual workflow until the accountable owner resolves the approval.

Keep customer data out of unapproved tools

Do not enter confidential or personal customer information into unapproved tools. Until the tool and intended data use are approved, prepare with fictional enquiries and approved public facts.

Set the measures before you start

Chatbase’s customer-service guide recommends tracking response time, escalation and quality. Use the proposed measures below for your draft-only pilot, without treating vendor claims as benchmarks.

Compare the whole task

Your baseline is the current manual process measured before introducing AI. Compare similar routine enquiries using identical start and finish points. Assisted handling time includes preparation, prompting, waiting that occupies staff, review, correction, handover and sending. Track setup and training separately, but include them in total pilot effort. Generation speed alone is not a fair comparison.

Calculate draft accuracy as drafts whose factual claims and necessary instructions match approved sources without factual correction, divided by all drafts reviewed. Record serious errors separately.

Calculate escalation frequency as cases requiring an additional human decision or handoff, divided by all cases entering the pilot workflow. Routine draft review is not escalation. Record reasons and missed required escalations: a lower rate can conceal failures to seek help.

Total pilot cost is incremental tool and usage charges plus staff time at a declared hourly cost. Include all pilot effort, including escalations, without counting staff minutes twice. Show cash spending and labour cost separately.

Decide what would justify continuing

Set numerical thresholds for handling time, draft accuracy, escalation performance and cost before testing. Specify critical safety failures and approval breaches that require an immediate stop, alongside case, time and spending limits. If a stop condition occurs, return to the manual process and investigate before proposing another trial.

Continue only when the agreed quality, safety, time and cost conditions are met. If too few eligible enquiries arrive before the deadline, record an inconclusive result. Extending the trial requires a new decision. A small sample can inform your next local decision; it cannot establish a general productivity claim.

A hypothetical pilot for routine reply drafts

Suppose a small software startup chooses reply drafting for recurring questions about exporting reports. These illustrative limits and thresholds are not industry standards, tested results or MLAI customer evidence. Drafting suits this workload better than enquiry sorting or internal lookup because questions repeat and maintained public instructions provide a narrow source set.

The founder owns the pilot, excluding account-specific troubleshooting and all mandatory-escalation cases described above. Before assisted testing, the team measures comparable manual handling times, leaving the baseline result blank until measured.

The proposed limits are two weeks, 20 eligible draft cases, four hours of total staff time and A$50 in incremental tool charges. At an assumed labour cost of A$50 per hour, the combined budget ceiling is A$250. These budget choices do not represent vendor prices or predicted expenditure.

The team prepares fictional questions and a dated, approved public help-page extract. After recording tool and data approvals, it enters only approved, non-identifying task text from eligible live enquiries into the approved tool. The founder checks every draft against the extract, corrects it and manually sends the final reply. The AI receives no inbox send permission. Anything outside scope goes to the named human decision-maker.

The record uses the handling-time, accuracy, escalation and cost measures above. Setup and training count towards the staff-time limit.

Before starting, the founder records the continue conditions: at least a 20% reduction in median total handling time against the measured baseline, at least 19 of 20 drafts factually correct without correction, no missed mandatory escalations and costs within the agreed limits. An unplanned handoff rate above 20% prompts a scope review, never pressure to avoid necessary escalation.

The founder handles rollback and investigation if a stop condition occurs. Time or spending limits also end testing. The output is a proposed pilot record ready for approval, with results unfilled. Meeting the conditions would justify considering another bounded test, not automatically launching a public chatbot.

Take a draft plan to your next conversation

Keep your pilot plan in draft until the named owner resolves outstanding approvals. You can discuss the chosen use case or documented decision to defer before committing money or connecting customer systems.

Ask peers about their own trials: which corrections consumed the most time, which vendor data controls did they verify, and what made them stop or narrow the trial? Use their answers to question your assumptions. Another business’s experience is not proof that your plan will work.

Explore MLAI events for optional peer learning. Availability, format and cost depend on the organiser’s event page. Attendance does not guarantee one-to-one implementation advice or replace running a pilot.

FAQ

What if our FAQ pages disagree?

Resolve conflicting FAQ pages before including those questions in the pilot. Name a person responsible for the source material and use a dated set of approved facts; the AI must not decide which policy is correct.

Does reviewing every reply count as escalation?

No. Routine review checks every draft before sending; escalation requires an additional human decision or handoff. Refunds, complaints, sensitive enquiries and unsupported answers must go to the named human decision-maker.

What if too few enquiries arrive before the pilot ends?

Record an inconclusive result if too few eligible enquiries arrive before the agreed deadline. Make a new decision before extending the trial. A small sample can inform a local next step but cannot establish a general productivity claim.

Does faster drafting mean the pilot saved money?

No. Faster drafting alone does not establish savings because preparation, review, corrections and handovers also take staff time. Calculate total pilot cost using incremental tool charges and staff time at a declared hourly cost, including setup and training.

Next Step

Get in touch about MLAI Studio

Browse testimonials and case studies from MLAI Studio, understand how MLAI Studio works, the price per month and how many builder hours that buys you.

Explore MLAI Studio

References

  • Artificial intelligence (AI) | business.gov.au
  • Guidance on privacy and the use of commercially available AI products | OAIC
  • AI in Customer Service: Use Cases, Examples & Benefits
  • 15 Examples of AI in Customer Service to Boost Efficiency
  • ChatGPT for Small Business | Workshop Resource Hub - Resource | OpenAI Academy
  • AI & Machine Learning Events in Australia | MLAI

Require the reviewer to check every reply against approved sources and correct it before sending, consistent with business.gov.au’s advice to verify AI-generated information against trustworthy sources.
claim_bindings.support_excerpt: However, don't assume that an AI summary is 100% accurate. Always check AI-generated information against a trustworthy source before you rely on it.

claim_bindings.claim_text: Refunds, complaints, sensitive enquiries and answers the sources cannot support must go to the named human decision-maker.
Keep sending under human control: the AI must not independently promise a refund, approve an exception or make another commitment to a customer.
If an enquiry cannot be prepared within the agreed data boundaries, keep it in the existing manual workflow until the accountable owner resolves the approval.
Chatbase’s customer-service guide recommends tracking response time, escalation and quality.
claim_bindings.support_excerpt: Strong AI support rollouts track response time, escalation rate, CSAT, reopen rate, and AI customer service statistics that show whether automation is improving support quality.

claim_bindings.claim_text: Use the proposed measures below for your draft-only pilot, without treating vendor claims as benchmarks.
Your baseline is the current manual process measured before introducing AI.
Compare similar routine enquiries using identical start and finish points.
Assisted handling time includes preparation, prompting, waiting that occupies staff, review, correction, handover and sending.
Track setup and training separately, but include them in total pilot effort.
Generation speed alone is not a fair comparison.
Calculate draft accuracy as drafts whose factual claims and necessary instructions match approved sources without factual correction, divided by all drafts reviewed.
Record serious errors separately.
Calculate escalation frequency as cases requiring an additional human decision or handoff, divided by all cases entering the pilot workflow.
Routine draft review is not escalation.
Record reasons and missed required escalations: a lower rate can conceal failures to seek help.
Total pilot cost is incremental tool and usage charges plus staff time at a declared hourly cost.
Include all pilot effort, including escalations, without counting staff minutes twice.
Show cash spending and labour cost separately.
Set numerical thresholds for handling time, draft accuracy, escalation performance and cost before testing.
Specify critical safety failures and approval breaches that require an immediate stop, alongside case, time and spending limits.
If a stop condition occurs, return to the manual process and investigate before proposing another trial.
Continue only when the agreed quality, safety, time and cost conditions are met.
If too few eligible enquiries arrive before the deadline, record an inconclusive result.
Extending the trial requires a new decision.
A small sample can inform your next local decision; it cannot establish a general productivity claim.
Suppose a small software startup chooses reply drafting for recurring questions about exporting reports.
These illustrative limits and thresholds are not industry standards, tested results or MLAI customer evidence.
Drafting suits this workload better than enquiry sorting or internal lookup because questions repeat and maintained public instructions provide a narrow source set.
The founder owns the pilot, excluding account-specific troubleshooting and all mandatory-escalation cases described above.
Before assisted testing, the team measures comparable manual handling times, leaving the baseline result blank until measured.
The proposed limits are two weeks, 20 eligible draft cases, four hours of total staff time and A$50 in incremental tool charges.
At an assumed labour cost of A$50 per hour, the combined budget ceiling is A$250.
These budget choices do not represent vendor prices or predicted expenditure.
The team prepares fictional questions and a dated, approved public help-page extract.
After recording tool and data approvals, it enters only approved, non-identifying task text from eligible live enquiries into the approved tool.
The founder checks every draft against the extract, corrects it and manually sends the final reply.
The AI receives no inbox send permission.
Anything outside scope goes to the named human decision-maker.
The record uses the handling-time, accuracy, escalation and cost measures above.
Setup and training count towards the staff-time limit.

Before starting, the founder records the continue conditions: at least a 20% reduction in median total handling time against the measured baseline, at least 19 of 20 drafts factually correct without correction, no missed mandatory escalations and costs within the agreed limits.
An unplanned handoff rate above 20% prompts a scope review, never pressure to avoid necessary escalation.
The founder handles rollback and investigation if a stop condition occurs.
Time or spending limits also end testing.
The output is a proposed pilot record ready for approval, with results unfilled.
Meeting the conditions would justify considering another bounded test, not automatically launching a public chatbot.
Keep your pilot plan in draft until the named owner resolves outstanding approvals.
You can discuss the chosen use case or documented decision to defer before committing money or connecting customer systems.
Ask peers about their own trials: which corrections consumed the most time, which vendor data controls did they verify, and what made them stop or narrow the trial?
Use their answers to question your assumptions.
Another business’s experience is not proof that your plan will work.
Explore MLAI events for optional peer learning.
Availability, format and cost depend on the organiser’s event page.
